item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 252324
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll, and
on Tropical Storm Iselle, located several hundred miles west of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula. The National
Hurricane Center has issued the last advisory on the Remnants of
Julio, located well west of the southern tip of the Baja California
Peninsula.

Central East Pacific:
A tropical wave located well to the south of southwestern Mexico is
producing a large area of showers and thunderstorms. This system is
gradually becoming better organized, and environmental conditions
appear favorable for continued development. A tropical depression is
expected to form in the next two or three days while it moves
generally west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, well offshore of
Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...60 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Western East Pacific:
A weak and small area of low pressure located well to the
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands is producing some
disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Environmental conditions
appear conducive for gradual development, and a tropical depression
is likely to form late this week or early this weekend while the
system drifts northeastward, then turns to the west-northwest.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

Well Offshore of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form this weekend well south of
southern Mexico. Environmental conditions should support some
gradual development of this system, and a tropical depression could
form by early next week while it moves westward to
west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian
Islands late this week or over the weekend. Some gradual
development is possible by early next week while the system moves
slowly to the west-northwest, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian
Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Cangialosi/Katz/Evans

item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...ISELLE WEAKENS SLIGHTLY... As of 8:00 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 the center of Iselle was located near 21.3, -122.5 with movement WNW at 9 mph. The minimum central pressure was 996 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 50 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Iselle Public Advisory Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026 
000
WTPZ34 KNHC 260231
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Iselle Advisory Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
800 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026
 
...ISELLE WEAKENS SLIGHTLY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM PDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...21.3N 122.5W
ABOUT 815 MI...1310 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...996 MB...29.42 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Iselle was
located near latitude 21.3 North, longitude 122.5 West. Iselle is
moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h), and this
general motion is expected for the next couple of days, with a turn
towards the west possible late on Wednesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 50 mph (85 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Weakening is forecast, and Iselle could become a 
post-tropical cyclone on Thursday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 230 miles (370 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 996 mb (29.42 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Iselle are affecting the west coast of the
Baja California Peninsula, and will continue for a couple more days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Papin

item.title: Tropical Storm Iselle Forecast Discussion Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 260232
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Iselle Discussion Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
800 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that Iselle continues to be sheared and 
that the low-level circulation is becoming more detached from the 
mid-level center. As such, the deep convection is still located away 
from the center of the storm, which is a strong indication that the 
cyclone is continuing to weaken. Water Vapor imagery also shows that 
dry air is intruding far into the core of the cyclone as well. While 
the most recent subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB was 
at CI 3.5/55 kt, the objective UW-CMISS estimates are lower and 
range from 33-45 kt. Thus, based on the available data, the initial 
intensity has been set to 45 kt for this advisory.
 
Further weakening is anticipated due to continued shear, 
progressively cooler water and increasing dry air entrainment near 
the core of the cyclone. The GFS and ECMWF simulated satellite 
imagery show the cyclone becoming devoid of organized deep 
convection in 24 to 36 h. Given the current appearance of the 
storm, it is possible that Iselle could become a post-tropical 
remnant low sooner and dissipate faster than indicated in the 
forecast. The current NHC intensity forecast is very similar to the 
previous one, with minor adjustments towards the end of the 
forecast period. 

Trends from the most recent satellite fixes show that the Iselle 
continues to move to the west-northwest around 7 kt. A ridge from 
the southern United States is expected to extend westward and should 
keep the system moving towards the west-northwest. As the storm 
weakens, it should turn more westward due to the low-level flow 
steering the shallow cyclone. The current NHC track is very similiar 
to the previous track, with only slight adjustments to the previous 
forecast.  
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  26/0300Z 21.3N 122.5W   45 KT  50 MPH
 12H  26/1200Z 21.6N 123.7W   40 KT  45 MPH
 24H  27/0000Z 22.3N 125.5W   35 KT  40 MPH

 60H  28/1200Z 23.8N 131.4W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW

$$
Forecaster Katz/Papin

item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...JULIO DISSIPATES... ...THIS IS THE LAST ADVISORY... As of 2:00 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 the center of Julio was located near 21.0, -119.5 with movement N at 25 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1003 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 45 mph.

item.title: Remnants of Julio Public Advisory Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026 
312 
WTPZ35 KNHC 252038
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Remnants Of Julio Advisory Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP102026
200 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026
 
...JULIO DISSIPATES...
...THIS IS THE LAST ADVISORY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...21.0N 119.5W
ABOUT 630 MI...1010 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 350 DEGREES AT 25 MPH...41 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1003 MB...29.62 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the remnants of Julio were located near 
latitude 21.0 North, longitude 119.5 West. The remnants are moving 
toward the north near 25 mph (41 km/h) and are expected to move 
northwestward into the circulation of Iselle tonight.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts.
Weakening is expected as the remnants decay tonight.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles (150 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1003 mb (29.62 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane 
Center on this system.  For additional information on the remnants 
of Julio, please see High Seas Forecasts issued by the National 
Weather Service, under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN01 
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

 
$$
Forecaster Blake/Evans
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Remnants of Julio Forecast Discussion Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 252040
TCDEP5
 
Remnants Of Julio Discussion Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP102026
200 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026

Satellite and microwave data indicate that the circulation of Julio 
has opened up into a trough of low pressure.  Thus, it is no 
longer a tropical cyclone, and this is the last NHC advisory.  The 
initial wind speed is set to 40 kt, consistent with the ASCAT-B pass 
from a few hours ago.  The remnant vorticity should wrap into the 
circulation of Tropical Storm Iselle and totally lose any identity 
soon.

For additional information on the remnants please see High Seas
Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service, under AWIPS
header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN01 KWBC, and on the web at
ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  25/2100Z 21.0N 119.5W   40 KT  45 MPH...REMNANTS OF
 12H  26/0600Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Blake/Evans
